overall: The AG found a violation for posting the March 23 meeting notice in a bulletin board location not visible 24 hours a day. No violation was found on the date/time stamp, the posting-method description, or the minutes allegations.

allegations.summary: Notice of the March 23 meeting was posted on a Town Hall bulletin board not accessible to the public 24 hours a day.
allegations.key_passage: As the Committee acknowledges, the bulletin board at Town Hall did not comply with the Open Meeting Law's requirement that notices be posted in a manner conspicuously visible to the public 24 hours a day.

allegations.summary: The website version of the meeting notice allegedly lacked the date and time it was posted.
allegations.key_passage: The notice posted on the bulletin board—the official posting method at the time—did conspicuously record the date and time of its posting.

allegations.summary: A description of the Town's official notice posting method was allegedly not publicly visible 24 hours a day.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Town had not adopted the website as the official notice posting method until the day this complaint was filed, we find no violation.

allegations.summary: The Committee allegedly failed to create minutes of the March 23 meeting, which was filed hours after the meeting ended.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements
